drivingQuestion: Do R' Yehuda and R' Yishmael hold one and the same view about the status of a bird's down?
outcomeNote: R' Yoḥanan's equation stands unopposed inside this unit; Rava blocks it with דילמא לא היא in the next one.

segments.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אִם נִיטְּלָה הַנּוֹצָה – פְּסוּלָה. אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אָמְרוּ דָּבָר אֶחָד. רַבִּי יְהוּדָה – הָא דַּאֲמַרַן, רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל – דִּתְנַן: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אוֹמֵר: הַנּוֹצָה מִצְטָרֶפֶת.
segments.en: § The mishna states: «Rabbi Yehuda says: If the down» covering its body «was removed,» it is a tereifa and «unfit» for consumption, like an animal whose hide was removed. With regard to this, «Rabbi Yoḥanan says: Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Yishmael said the same thing. Rabbi Yehuda» said «that which we said» here, that the removal of the feathers is like removal of the hide. «Rabbi Yishmael» agrees, «as we learned» in a baraita: «Rabbi Yishmael says: The down joins» the flesh to constitute an olive-bulk for purposes of piggul. If a priest pinches the nape of the neck of a bird with intent to consume a combined olive-bulk of its meat and its down beyond the permitted time, the offering is rendered piggul. Evidently, both Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Yishmael agree that the down of a bird is considered like the hide of an animal.
